title: Kingdom of Greece
capsule: The Kingdom of Greece was restored after liberation from Axis occupation when a regency under Archbishop Damaskinos was established in December 1944, and a rigged — or at least strongly royalist — plebiscite in September 1946 returned King George II to the throne. The kingdom weathered a brutal civil war (1946–1949) in which communist insurgents were defeated with American support under the Truman Doctrine. King Paul (r. 1947–1964) and his son Constantine II presided over rapid economic growth in the 1950s–1960s. The military coup of 21 April 1967, led by a junta of colonels, suspended constitutional government and effectively ended the monarchy's active role; Constantine fled into exile in December 1967 after a failed counter-coup, and the junta formally abolished the monarchy by referendum in 1973.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the post-1945 Kingdom of Greece is well defined by internationally recognized borders; the dataset's start date of 1945 reflects the end of Axis occupation rather than the formal restoration of the monarchy.
